5 تقلّد , (K,) and تقلّدت, (S,) and تقلّد قِلَادَةً, (L,) and تقلّدتها, (Msb,) He put on his neck, or attired himself with, a قلادة [or necklace], and she did the same. (S, L, Msb, K.) ―
-b2- تقلّد السَّيْفَ (S, A, L) He hung upon himself the sword, putting its suspensory belt or cord upon his neck [or shoulder]. (A.) A poet says, “يَا لَيْتَ زَوْجَكِ قَدْ غَدَا
مُتَقَلِّدًا سَيْفًا وَرُمْحًا
” [Would that thy husband had gone hanging upon him a sword and bearing a spear]: he means, وَحَامِلًا رُمْحًا. (S, L.) [See a similar saying voce جَدَعَ.] ―
-b3- تقلّد العَمَلَ (tropical:) [He became invested with an office of administration, or a prefecture]. (A.) ―
-b4- تقلّد الأَمْرَ (tropical:) He took, or imposed, upon himself, or undertook, the thing, or affair; (L;) syn. اِلْتَزَمَهُ. (JK.) See Ham. p. 127.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
